title: FactoryEvidenceReceipt
description: One immutable observation recorded against a Factory outcome (spec-factory.md §2 'record immutable evidence observations'; §5 'immutable evidence receipts'). Never mutated or deleted once recorded — a correction is a new receipt, never an edit of this one. Modeled from the repo's own proven `factory.domain.EvidenceInput`/`add_evidence`, not invented ahead of what ships. Fulfils demand `factory-20260911-interface-extraction` criterion 1.

kind.description: Which workflow step this evidence closes. Which kinds a given outcome actually requires depends on its `kind` (bug/feature/new-app) — this schema does not re-derive that mapping, only enumerates every kind Factory's own workflows can produce.

criteria.description: The acceptance criterion IDs (from the outcome's `criteria`) this evidence covers. Required and non-empty for `implementation`/`tests`/`live`; may be empty for outcome-level kinds like `merge`/`deployment` that are not per-criterion.

result.description: Only a `passed` receipt at the current candidate revision counts toward completion (see `factory.domain.receipt`); a `failed` receipt is retained, never discarded, as the honest record of what was tried.

revision.description: The candidate revision this evidence was observed at. Required (and must equal the outcome's current `candidate`) for revision-scoped kinds (`implementation`, `tests`, `merge`, `acceptance`, `deployment`, `live`); empty string otherwise.

deployment.description: The exact deployment identifier — never only an app URL — for `deployment`/`live` evidence; empty string for other kinds.

summary.description: Human-readable account of what was observed.

source.description: Where this observation came from (a CI run URL, a transcript reference, a manual check description).

observer.description: Who or what recorded this evidence.

provenance.description: How this evidence was authorized. A fixed const, not a free-text field: spec-factory.md open question 3 states plainly that in this slice every receipt is an explicit owner attestation, never an automatic CI/deployment verification — the contract states that structurally rather than trusting a caller to type it correctly. A future machine-verified provenance is an additive enum value, not a shape change.

planHash.description: SHA-256 over the outcome's approved scope at the moment this evidence was recorded — binds the receipt to one exact plan, so a later plan revision can never silently inherit an old receipt (see `factory.domain.plan_hash`/`receipt`).

hash.description: SHA-256 over this receipt's own full recorded content (including `id`/`recordedAt`) — the receipt's own tamper-evident content digest, distinct from `planHash`.
